# Discovery evidence (generated by `python -m evaluation.discovery_analysis`)

Source: `data/development_tickets.json` (500 tickets) and `data/documentation.json` (29 articles). History fields describe what CloudServe's human operation achieved; labels describe what should have happened.

## E9. Text duplication and label consistency

Distinct ticket bodies: 216 of 500. Bodies that appear more than once: 78 (covering 362 tickets).

Highest accuracy any system reading only the text could reach (identical texts must get identical predictions):

| label | ceiling |
|---|---|
| intent | 100.0% |
| urgency | 73.0% |
| answerable_from_docs | 86.6% |
| expected_route | 88.8% |
| expected_doc_ids | 78.2% |

## E10. Routing policy implied by the labels

| expected_route | answerable | must_not_auto_respond | tickets |
|---|---|---|---|
| auto_respond | True | False | 311 |
| escalate | False | False | 87 |
| escalate | False | True | 56 |
| escalate | True | False | 15 |
| escalate | True | True | 31 |

The 15 answerable, policy-permitted tickets labelled `escalate` are all urgency=high and intent in ['database_issue', 'performance_degradation'].
